newsitem.title: USA: University of California considers budget proposal.
newsitem.headline: University of California considers budget proposal.

text.p: The University of California's 1997-1998 proposed budget plan anticipates a 4.0 percent increase in state funding and a total student fee increase of just under 10 percent, university officials said.
The university said the budget recommendations for 1997-1998 would be presented for discussion on Thursday to the University of California's board of regents.
The regents are expected to act on the proposed budget at their November meeting.

Under the budget plan, the University of California would receive a $136 million or a 4.8 percent funding increase in 1997-1998, with $80.5 million coming from a projected 4.0 percent increase in state general fund support. The remainder would come from fee increases.
The budget plan would bring state support, excluding debt service on bonds, to $2.04 billion, slightly less than what the university system received from the state in 1989-1990.
University officials said the recommended fee increase would generate about $49.5 million in new revenue, with a third or about $16.5 million set aside for financial aid.
The rest would cover fixed cost increases in student programs and help to fund the general operating budget.
The budget plan also includes an instructional technology fee and an increase in out-of-state tuition.
University officials said any action on general fees would take place after Gov. Pete Wilson presents his state budget proposal in January.
